A1.evidence: The paper's own scripts are retrievable by identifier over a standard protocol: DOI resolution to an open Zenodo record (pack access_right "open", http_status 200) and HTTPS clone/download from the public GitHub repository (pack github record resolved, archived_flag false, default_branch main, pushed_at 2024-03-14).

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS/DOI retrieval of an open-access record; source is R code in a plain-text open language, requiring no proprietary client or paid subscription. Pack shows both endpoints resolving anonymously (http_status 200).

A1_2.evidence: Fully open code deposit requiring no authentication (pack access_right "open"); under the v2.1 A1.2 open case this satisfies the sub-principle - authentication is supported by the protocol where needed and none is needed. A2.evidence: Row 2 (Zenodo) entitlement: metadata always publicly accessible, tombstone page with DOI and URL retained on withdrawal; corroborated by the resolved DataCite record. F1.evidence: The paper's own analysis scripts (principal code artefact) carry a Zenodo DOI: "All data and R scripts are available on https://github.com/ercrema/diffusionCurve and permanently archived on https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10782942" (p. 7). F2.evidence: Pack: metadata_record true at both DataCite and Zenodo for the software deposit, with populated publisher (Zenodo), publication_year (2024), resource_type (Software), licence (cc-by-4.0), access_right (open) and state (findable). F3.evidence: Pack: identifier_in_metadata true in the DataCite record (10.5281/zenodo.10782942) and the Zenodo record (version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10816946 with concept_doi 10.5281/zenodo.10782942) - the software metadata explicitly includes its identifier.

F4.evidence: Software deposit indexed in DataCite (pack datacite record, http_status 200, state "findable") and searchable on Zenodo (pack zenodo record, record_id_on_service 10816946).

I1.evidence: Code is written in a formal, open, broadly shared language: "Both the hierarchical model described in equations [5-6] and the random walk ICAR model were implemented using the NIMBLE (de Valpine et al., 2017, 2020) probabilistic programming language in R (R Core Team, 2020) and the nimbleCarbon R package (Crema, 2022b)" (p. 5-6). Plain-text R/NIMBLE source, no proprietary or binary-only distribution.

I2.evidence: Looked for software-metadata vocabularies that are themselves FAIR (CodeMeta, schema.org SoftwareSourceCode, CITATION.cff-declared terms) in the paper, the availability statement, and the pack's metadata fields; none is evidenced. The Zenodo/DataCite record supplies a resourceType only, which is a schema field, not a controlled software vocabulary.

I3.evidence: Per the v2.1 aggregation rule, third-party dependencies enter code scoring through citation quality: the Methods state the relation and identify the dependencies, with a PID for the principal one - "implemented using the NIMBLE (de Valpine et al., 2017, 2020) probabilistic programming language in R (R Core Team, 2020) and the nimbleCarbon R package (Crema, 2022b)" (p. 5-6), with the reference list giving NIMBLE as https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1211190, nimbleCarbon at version 0.2.0, and the AADR data resource as https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/FFIDCW. R1.evidence: The implementation is richly described: priors given explicitly (r ~ Exponential(100); mu ~ Beta(2,2); phi ~ Gamma(5,0.1), equations 10-12), the truncated normal prior on m with per-dataset means/SDs, MCMC configuration for both models ("four chains, each with 1 million iterations (half discarded as burn-in) and with thinning set to 50"), convergence diagnostics ("Gelman-Rubin statistic ... agreement indices"), and posterior predictive check procedure ("1000 randomly selected parameters from the joint posterior distributions") - p. 6.

R1_1.evidence: Pack: the Zenodo/DataCite software record carries licences ["cc-by-4.0"] with licence_conflicts empty - an identified, machine-readable licence, satisfying the v2.1 requirement that a mandatory platform licence field is not itself sufficient. The GitHub mirror returns an empty licence list; under Row 5 that is a detection null rather than a competing assertion about the same artefact, so the most-restrictive rule is not engaged. (Noted: CC-BY-4.0 is a content rather than software licence, but it is clear, accessible and operative.)

R1_2.evidence: Provenance of the code artefact is documented through versioned deposit and execution detail: pack shows a concept DOI (10.5281/zenodo.10782942) with a distinct version DOI (10.5281/zenodo.10816946) and a dated GitHub state (pushed_at 2024-03-14T08:55:47Z); the paper records the runtime stack and versions (R, NIMBLE, nimbleCarbon 0.2.0), model settings, priors, and the IntCal20 calibration curve used for all models (p. 7). CRediT statement (p. 9) attributes "Software" to E.R. Crema.

R1_3.evidence: Qualifying via route (a) of the v2.1 R1.3 section - the deposit is described under the DataCite generic metadata schema (pack datacite record resolved for the software DOI; Row 2 entitlement). No code-specific route is evidenced in the paper or the pack: there is no statement of R package structure, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or community review (the deposit is a research compendium, not a CRAN/JOSS/rOpenSci-reviewed package; nimbleCarbon is a separate, cited dependency, not the deposited artefact). Score therefore rests solely on the DataCite route.

I1.evidence: The deposited data are the direct inputs to the R/NIMBLE analysis scripts archived with them (paper p. 6: models "were implemented using the NIMBLE ... probabilistic programming language in R ... and the nimbleCarbon R package"; p. 7: "All data and R scripts are available on ... diffusionCurve"), so the data are held in machine-parseable, programmatically-consumed formats rather than PDF/word tables. Zenodo resource_type recorded as Software for the combined deposit.

I2.evidence: Looked for controlled vocabularies or ontologies with PIDs governing the data fields (ARIADNEplus, PeriodO, Getty AAT, CIDOC-CRM, Darwin Core) in the Methods, in the availability statement, and in the pack's metadata fields; none is named. Site, taxon (rice, wheat, barley, hazelnut), and period terms are free-text; the only standard invoked is IntCal20 (Reimer et al., 2020), a methodological calibration standard that expressly does not qualify under the v2.1 R1.3/I2 boundary.

I3.evidence: No qualified, typed PID references from the deposited data to the resources it derives from. Upstream databases are cited bibliographically only - "Japanese dates were collated from the radiocarbon databases of Japan (Kudo et al., 2023) and the rice radiocarbon database used in (Crema et al., 2022)" (p. 5); burial dates "collated from different published sources and databases (Bevan et al., 2017; Bloxam, 2020; ... Willis et al., 2016)" (p. 5) - without dataset DOIs in those in-text/reference entries (only Mallick and Reich, 2023 carries a data DOI). The pack records no relatedIdentifier set beyond the internal concept/version DOI pair, which is versioning of the same object, not a qualified reference to another resource. Conjunctive scoring across principal datasets therefore fails.

R1.evidence: Methods 4.1 describes each principal dataset with a plurality of relevant attributes: "We examined a total of 1479 14C dates on seed remains from Japan (n = 551, from 215 sites ...) and Britain (n = 928, from 314 sites ...)", with sources, the cumulative-probability filters ("equal to or larger than 0.5 for the interval 4000-1700 cal BP"; "0.99 for the interval 5500-2000 cal BP"), material classes (rice n = 203; wild nuts n = 348; wheat n = 261; barley n = 130; hazelnut n = 537; cremation n = 1417; inhumation n = 1119), spatial exclusions (Hokkaido, Ryukyu), and mapped site distributions (Fig. 1).

R1_1.evidence: Licence identified at the hosting service: pack DataCite and Zenodo records both record licences ["cc-by-4.0"] for the deposit, with licence_conflicts empty. The paper asserts no separate licence for the data, so no same-artefact disagreement arises; the GitHub mirror returns an empty licence list, which under Row 5 is a detection null ("Detection is not a usable SPDX identifier") and not a competing licence assertion, so the most-restrictive rule is not triggered. CC-BY-4.0 is an identified, machine-readable licence, not merely a populated platform field.

R1_2.evidence: Derivation is documented end to end: named upstream sources for each case study (Methods 4.1.2, 4.1.3), explicit chronological filtering rules and thresholds, calibration provenance ("We used the IntCal20 curve for all models (Reimer et al., 2020) using the calibration process defined in equation [3]", p. 7), and processing environment/parameters (NIMBLE in R with nimbleCarbon 0.2.0; "four chains, each with 1 million iterations (half discarded as burn-in) and with thinning set to 50"; ICAR "four chains, each with 100,000 iterations (20,000 of which were discarded for burn-in), with parameters collected every four steps"). The deposit is versioned (concept 10.5281/zenodo.10782942 / version 10.5281/zenodo.10816946).

R1_3.evidence: Qualifying route (a) of the v2.1 R1.3 section - generic metadata schema: the deposit is described under DataCite, evidenced at rung (i) by the resolved DataCite record (publisher, publicationYear 2024, resourceType, identifier, rights) and entitled at rung (ii) by platform table Row 2. No domain route applies: no ARIADNEplus/CIDOC-CRM/Darwin Core vocabulary is used and the deposit is not in an accredited domain repository (not ADS/DANS/tDAR). IntCal20 is methodological and is expressly excluded.
